findings.summary: just parses trailing words on a command line as additional recipes to run when the preceding recipe takes no parameters. Verified with the repo's own just 1.58.0: `just lint publish-pypi` prints and would run `bazel run //:ruff -- check .` then `bazel build //packaging:wheel` then `bazel run //packaging:wheel.publish -- --repository pypi` -- a real PyPI publish. The full command string 'just lint publish-pypi' prefix-matches allow rule Bash(just lint:*) and never contains 'publish-pypi' as a separately-parsed subcommand, so it cannot be caught by Claude Code's operator-aware compound-command splitting (there is no shell operator here at all -- this is just's own argument parsing). Same mechanism via typecheck, fmt-check, and validate-catalog. This diff makes an unprompted PyPI publish reachable, inverting the slice's stated purpose.

The test recipe interpolates its variadic {{args}} unquoted into a shell line (`bazel test //tests/... {{args}}`). Verified: `just test '&& echo INJECTED'` produces and would execute `bazel test //tests/... && echo INJECTED` -- including `just test '&& just publish-pypi'`. The command string 'just test ...' still prefix-matches allow Bash(just test:*) as a single quoted argument; exploitability depends on whether Claude Code's own splitter is quote-aware, but the shell-injection mechanism inside just itself is verified regardless.

This allow list ships in the bundle to every downstream repo that installs CoDev (confirmed by the diff's own byte-identity test). Entries like Bash(just test:*)/Bash(just lint:*) pre-approve whatever a downstream project's own justfile recipes happen to do, including their own unquoted argument interpolation -- a decision made on behalf of repositories whose recipes CoDev cannot see. Narrowing the entries to resolve SEC-1/SEC-2 likely resolves most of this, but the bundled-vs-local distinction deserves an explicit decision.

git diff/log/show accept --output=<file>, which writes and truncates an arbitrary path -- verified: git diff --output=victim.txt wholesale-replaced an existing file's content with diff text. So git diff --output=.claude/settings.json (or any source file) is a prompt-free arbitrary-file-overwrite primitive, sidestepping the Edit tool entirely. The PreToolUse hooks are not a backstop (require_plan.py fails open by its own docstring, and git diff isn't in ADR-0002's mutation-prefix list). The other allow entries (codev next/task check/task log, lint, fmt-check, validate-catalog, gh run view) were independently confirmed read-only.

The test suite pins deny membership, defaultMode, hook count, and bundle/installed parity, but asserts nothing about the allow list's actual contents. A future edit adding Bash(just:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(gh:*), or Bash(codev:*) passes every existing assertion. An exact-equality check on the allow list (and exact-set rather than assertIn on deny) would force a deliberate edit and a reviewer's eye before the boundary widens.

AGENTS.md now says the publish prohibition 'is now enforced rather than merely stated' and deny 'refuses both recipes' -- false while SEC-1 stands, and an overclaim even once fixed: `just --justfile Justfile publish-pypi`, an env-prefixed invocation, or the underlying `bazel run //packaging:wheel.publish` all evade the deny pattern by name (though those at least fall back to a prompt, matching no allow rule). The defensible claim is 'removes the silent path for these exact recipe names,' not 'enforced.'

Same underlying gap as pr56-sec5, raised independently by correctness-tests-specialist: no test pins the allow list itself, which the accepted plan names as the primary risk ('a wrong allow widens that silently').

The plan's completion-evidence checklist includes a manual check that just publish-pypi is actually refused and that a routine turn prompts less; neither was exercised/recorded as evidence in this non-interactive build.

## Defect found by dogfooding, and fixed

Running `require_green.py` against its own change during manual verification

`tests/test_claude_hook.py` flagged all twenty pre-existing tests as "same
assertions as HEAD" -- true, and irrelevant, since nobody touched them. On
any real change this would have made the hook unusable. Fixed by carrying
each function's normalised body alongside its assertions and skipping
functions that are byte-identical to `HEAD`. Two regression tests pin both
directions (`test_ignores_untouched_tests_in_a_file_that_gained_a_new_one`,
`test_still_flags_a_touched_test_in_a_file_with_untouched_ones`).

installed -- leaving the block path, the most important behaviour this hook
has, effectively untested in CI. Replaced the dependency with a planted
`.tools/just` shim; the suite now runs 19 of 19 with zero skips.

findings.summary: [s1] New `python -m <name>` invocations run with cwd=repo_root and without `-P`, so a file at the repository root can shadow the intended module. Verified empirically: with `ruff.py` in cwd, `python3 -m ruff --version` printed the planted file's output; `python3 -P -m ruff --version` printed the real ruff version. The same applies to `[sys.executable, '-m', 'codev_workflow']`, where a repo-root `codev_workflow.py`/`codev_workflow/` would both execute and dictate the gate's allow/ask verdict, and to the `-m ruff|mypy|pytest|unittest` fallbacks the Stop hook runs. This path is introduced by this PR (the previous code resolved a bare `codev` from PATH, which does not include cwd on Unix). Exploiting it needs a repository whose contents the developer has not audited -- plausible when an agent session is pointed at a contributor branch or a submitted repo. Correction: add `-P` to every `[sys.executable, '-m', ...]` argv (requires-python is already >=3.11) or pass env with PYTHONSAFEPATH=1; test by planting `ruff.py` at a fixture repo root and asserting the hook still runs real ruff.

findings.summary: [s2] The formatter is invoked on explicitly-named paths without `--force-exclude`, and ruff applies `exclude`/`extend-exclude` to explicit paths only when that flag is set. Verified in this repository: `ruff format --check src/codev_workflow/bundle/.claude/hooks/require_green.py` reported '1 file would be reformatted' while the same command with `--force-exclude` reported 'No Python files found under the given path(s)'. So the hook rewrites files the project has deliberately declared off-limits to its own formatter -- here `src/codev_workflow/bundle`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, and notably `.codev/eval/tasks/*/repository`, which are evaluation fixture repositories whose exact bytes are the input to eval runs. `just fmt-check` will never notice, because it honours the exclusion. Correction: pass `--force-exclude`, and add a test that a path matched by the fixture repo's ruff `exclude` is left byte-identical after the hook runs.
[c2] The auto-discovered direct fallbacks turn a misconfigured environment into a hard `block`, which is the fail-closed direction the plan named as the high risk.
[c4] Every test that asserts `format_touched.py` actually formats anything is skipped in CI, so the hook's entire purpose is untested there.
[c3] Test functions are keyed by bare name, so two same-named methods in one file collapse and the pre-change check silently skips the touched one.

[s3] The formatter hook ships to every repository the bundle installs into and runs ruff whenever ruff is importable or on PATH, with no check that the target project actually uses ruff. `shutil.which('ruff')` will find a user-global ruff (pipx/uv/brew) in a project formatted by black, yapf, or nothing, and every Python file the agent touches there is silently restyled to ruff's defaults, mixing unrelated formatting churn into the developer's change. This is looser than the discipline `require_green.py:_checks` applies for exactly the same reason ('installs everywhere'), where a `just` recipe declared by the repository wins. Correction: require positive evidence the repo uses ruff -- a `fmt`/`format` just recipe, or a `[tool.ruff]` table / `ruff.toml` / `.ruff.toml` -- before formatting, and no-op (logging `degraded`) otherwise; test with a fixture repo that has ruff on PATH but no ruff configuration.
[c7] The formatter logs its no-op as `degraded`, the same label `codev health` reports as 'gate call(s) failed open ... allowed without being checked'.
[c5] Nothing pins that the two new hooks are wired at all; the existing settings assertion counts only `PreToolUse` and passes unchanged.

[s5] 'Run the repository's formatter, static checks, affected tests, and proportionate broader tests' is removed from the guidelines file the bundle ships to all four adapters, but the enforcement that replaces it (`require_green.py`) exists only under Claude Code. Antigravity, Junie, and OpenCode sessions therefore lose the instruction and gain nothing; what remains for them is 'Report the exact validation commands and their outcomes', which presumes a run it no longer asks for. AGENTS.md keeps a repo-specific line and marks it Claude-only, so the gap is visible there but not in the shared file. Correction: keep a one-line platform-neutral instruction to run the repository's checks in the shared guidelines (the net-bytes claim survives; the removed sentence was four lines), or move the retirement into the Claude-only `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
[c6] The health check that exists to catch a hook pointing at a missing script only scans `PreToolUse`, so it is blind to both hooks this slice adds.
[c9] Two tests assert weakly or structurally: one is misnamed and environment-dependent, the other pins source text rather than behaviour.

[s4] The Stop hook executes repository-resident code automatically and outside Claude Code's permission system: `_just_argv` prefers `repo_root/.tools/just{,.exe,.bat,.cmd}` over PATH, and the recipes it then runs (`just lint|typecheck|test`) are arbitrary command bodies from the checked-in Justfile; the gate hooks likewise prefer `repo_root/.venv/bin/codev`. The trust assumption ('opening a repo in a CoDev session means trusting its build files') is real and probably acceptable for this audience, but it is currently unstated and unauditable. Correction, cheap and testable: record the resolved argv in the `.codev/hooks/decisions.jsonl` pass/degraded records (only the check name is stored today), and state the trust assumption in the hook docstring and CHANGELOG entry so a developer reviewing an untrusted branch knows what end-of-turn will run.

findings.summary: The three new hooks each define their own byte-identical (or near-identical) ~20-line codev-next-json runner -- exactly the triplication this slice's own _gate_common.py extraction was justified by ending for the three existing gate hooks. Extract one shared codev_next(repo_root, *, timeout) into the shared module.

The module's docstring still says 'Shared plumbing for the PreToolUse gate hooks', which is now false for three of its six clients (restore_position.py, checkpoint_state.py, statusline.py use only codev_argv, not the gate machinery). Rename or restructure so the name matches the real dependency shape -- best done alongside fixing f1.

The skip reason says Decision 1 'is not yet resolved by the developer' and lists three still-open options, but the plan's completion evidence and CHANGELOG both record that it WAS resolved on 2026-09-12 (issue #69 filed). The skip text contradicts the record it documents, and since a skipped test is invisible in just test's normal output, this stale text is the only in-repo pointer a future reader gets.

The parent plan still states an unqualified '7,225 against a 7,500 ceiling -- 275 tokens of headroom' and 'every hook added must retire the prose it replaces, in the same slice' rule. This PR's own measurement (34,389 bytes over a 33,100-byte derived ceiling) disproves both, and scientific-gates builds next against a ledger row known to be wrong. The reorder got a dated note in this same file; the budget finding should too.

The strict-equality baseline-accuracy assertion subsumes the non-increase (<=) assertion -- the first can never fail without the second also failing, making the non-increase test dead as a detector. It also means any edit to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/guidelines/skill or agent descriptions now red-builds until the baseline JSON is hand-updated to match, which is close to what the hand-maintained ledger already cost. Collapse to one assertion with the intended semantics, or document that lockstep updating is deliberate.

The 'checkpoint.json' filename is an independently-defined string constant in four places (both hooks, both test files) with no single source of truth. Neither hook's own test does a writer-to-reader round trip, so renaming one side would silently break compaction recovery with a green suite. Move the constant into the shared module.

Still reads 'Same reasoning as _codev_argv in the gate hooks', a name that exists nowhere in the repository after this slice's rename to codev_argv. format_touched.py is already in this slice's allowed scope.

Three touched files are outside the plan's enumerated 'Allowed scope' list: .codev/instruction-budget-baseline.json, root BUILD.bazel, and docs/plans/claude-code-adapter-verification-first.md. Each is individually defensible (described by step 7, mechanically required by the new py_test target, and the reorder record respectively) but the list should be updated to match, since the completion checklist claims the diff stays inside it.

test_tolerates_an_unwritable_scratchpad asserts only returncode == 0, which passes vacuously if _next_position returns None (the write path it names is never reached). Assert result.stderr == '' (or absence of a traceback) so it actually catches a removed except OSError.

On Claude Code versions whose PreCompact payload predates the snake_case scratchpad_dir key (confirmed absent in the locally-installed 2.1.245, present in 2.1.269), the checkpoint path is silently inert -- no crash, but the feature's headline guarantee is version-gated in a way nothing in the repo asserts or documents.

A checkpoint dict lacking a 'position' key would render 'CoDev position: None'. Not reachable from real data (NextAction declares position/recommendation/reason non-optional), noted for completeness only.

'.claude/worktrees/' is absent from both the tracked .gitignore and the installer's managed GITIGNORE_BLOCK, and codev git commit's git add -A would stage a worktree as a gitlink if created there. Already mitigated in practice by Claude Code's own runtime-managed .git/info/exclude, so no live exposure on a current CLI, but cheap insurance for older installs.
